content_voiceover: This slide features the MajesTEC-3 trial, published in December twenty twenty five, which compared teclistamab plus daratumumab against standard daratumumab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone or daratumumab-bortezomib-dexamethasone in relapsed refractory myeloma. The overall survival benefit was substantial, thirty six month overall survival was eighty three point three percent with teclistamab-daratumumab compared to sixty five percent with the standard regimens, a highly significant difference. Alongside this trial data, the slide shows the NCCN recommendations for therapy after three or more prior lines of treatment. CAR T cell therapy, either ciltacabtagene autoleucel or idecabtagene vicleucel, is preferred. After at least four prior therapies including an anti-CD38 antibody, a proteasome inhibitor, and an immunomodulatory drug, bispecific antibodies become preferred options, elranatamab, linvoseltamab, talquetamab, and teclistamab. Other recommended options include high dose or fractionated cyclophosphamide, and after four or more prior therapies with refractoriness to at least two proteasome inhibitors, two immunomodulatory agents, and an anti-CD38 antibody, selinexor plus dexamethasone is an option. Finally, useful in certain circumstances includes belantamab mafodotin, bendamustine based combinations, and combining talquetamab with teclistamab.
keypoints: MajesTEC-3 showed teclistamab-daratumumab improved 36-month OS to 83.3% vs 65%
CAR T-cell therapy is preferred after 3 or more prior lines of therapy
Bispecific antibodies are preferred after 4+ lines including anti-CD38, PI, and IMiD exposure
Selinexor-dexamethasone is an option for penta-refractory disease
keypoint_voiceover: Take away that MajesTEC-3 demonstrated a clear overall survival advantage for teclistamab plus daratumumab, and that NCCN now positions CAR T cell therapy as preferred after three or more prior lines, with bispecific antibodies preferred once patients are refractory to an anti-CD38 antibody, a PI, and an IMiD.
